answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. Candidate agents must solve sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic steps before reaching an epoch zenith. This forces an attacker to expend scarce single-core processor time per identity instead of simulating an ocean of clones across a shifting dune of virtual machines. However, adversaries with high-frequency specialized silicon compute proofs faster, unfairly lowering their cost per generated identity.
